summary: Edward Albert Gait worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at University College London (~1880–1882), founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914, and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Amundsen was a Tibetologist and linguist. He held posts with the Tibetan Pioneer Mission (1893), the British and Foreign Bible Society as Superintendent for South-West China and Tibet (1903–1915), and Det Norske Misjonsforbund (1919–1924).

Edward Arthur Henry Blunt specialized in history/archaeology and Indology. Educated at Marlborough College, Corpus Christi College, Oxford (B.A.), and University College London, he served in the Indian Civil Service and the governments of the United Provinces and Uttar Pradesh.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and Oxford (M.A.), later serving as professor and librarian at East India Company College and in the Foreign Office.

Edward Byles Cowell worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Magdalen Hall under Horace Hayman Wilson and held professorships at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Cambridge, also heading Sanskrit College.

Edward C. Dimock Jr. specialized in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He earned degrees from Yale and Harvard, studying under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held positions at the University of Chicago and the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Edward Capps was a scholar of history/archaeology and linguistics. He studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg, and held academic posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley worked in history/archaeology and Indology. Educated at Haileybury and East India Company College, he entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842 and later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta and President of The Asiatic Society.

Edward Conze worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied across several German universities, completing a Ph.D. under Max Scheler at Cologne. His posts included teaching at the University of London, University of Washington, and various visiting professorships.

Edward Delavan Perry worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Professor and Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy at Columbia University from 1880 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. Educated at UCL and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke, he held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, and served as SOAS's administrator and Persian professor.

Edward Douglas Maclagan worked in history/archaeology and Indology. Educated at Winchester College and New College, Oxford, he later served as Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (1919–1924) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (1925–1928).

Edward Edwards specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Bala Theological College, Aberystwyth University under Hermann Ethé, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He worked as an Assistant at the British Museum and served on boards at the University of London.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale and in Europe under Burnouf, Bopp, Silvestre de Sacy, and Lassen. He became professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale and served as president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He held academic posts at LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and Oxford (1946–1970).
Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Geoffrey Parrinder worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Richmond College (1929–1932) and served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Ibadan (~1949–1958) before becoming Reader at King's College London in 1958.

Edward Granville Browne was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. Educated at Newcastle and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, Edward Henry Palmer, and William Wright, he held posts at Cambridge as Lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic.

Edward Green Balfour worked in Indology and other fields. Educated at Montrose Academy and the University of Edinburgh (~1831–1834), he founded the Government Museum in Chennai (1850) and the Mysore Museum (1866), and was a fellow of the University of Madras.
